data_points.claim: The reference cuts 12 times in 10 seconds — 72 cuts per minute, average shot 0.83s, shortest 0.62s, longest 2.5s (the final lockup).
data_points.source_name: OpenMontage video_analyzer scene detection on the supplied file

data_points.claim: Mask reveal — text hidden behind a shape that moves to expose it — is the technique most associated with cinematic type in 2026.
Per-character animation (each letter with its own timing) is what separates text that reveals from text that performs.

In risograph practice the registration spot colour is literally a crosshair swatch, and duotone is made by superimposing one colour on another — the crop-mark/two-accent look in the supplied posters is a real press artefact, not decoration.
Professional anime trailers mix graphic design, silhouettes, photographic texture, particles and bold typography, transforming the composition every few moments.
GSAP SplitText splits a heading into chars/words/lines for independently timed staggers; wrapping chars with overflow:hidden produces the masked slide-up reveal.

common_questions: How do you get a character to pass behind one letter and in front of the next?
How do you keep a 10-second cut-fest from reading as random noise?
How do you make code-rendered motion graphics look printed rather than screen-native?
How much can you cut before a shot stops registering at all?

misconceptions.myth: A reveal trailer needs generated video footage.
misconceptions.reality: The reference is almost entirely design layers — flat colour fields, type, particles and a cut-out subject. The only photographic elements are one macro eye and the character art. This is a composition job, not a video-generation job.
misconceptions.source: agent vision pass over the reference keyframes

misconceptions.reality: The reference spends 25% of its runtime on a single static end lockup. The cutting only reads as fast because it resolves into stillness.

audience_insights.knowledge_level: Design-literate short-form viewers. They will read 'movie poster' instantly from crop marks and a barcode, and they will notice if type and subject sit on the same flat layer.
pain_points: Kinetic type reels all look alike because everyone assembles the same stock presets
Print texture applied as a full-frame overlay reads as a filter, not as printing

angles_discovered.name: Cold Open — the procedural noir reveal
angles_discovered.hook: A man who never moves, in a layout that will not stop moving.
angles_discovered.why_now: Crime titles default to slow and moody; the reference's grammar is rapid-fire and graphic. Putting a motionless subject inside that grammar is the gap identified in landscape.underserved_gaps, and it is the one thing the reference cannot do because its character is an athlete.
grounded_in: The reference spends 25% of runtime on a static lockup
Mask reveal is the dominant cinematic type technique for 2026

angles_discovered.name: Press Sheet — the poster that prints itself
angles_discovered.hook: Four colour plates land one at a time until the poster exists.
angles_discovered.why_now: The registration crosshair and duotone superimposition are real press mechanics (data_points), so the motion has an honest internal logic instead of arbitrary transitions — and none of the surveyed kinetic-type content uses it.
grounded_in: Print artefacts are a persistent layer in the reference

angles_discovered.name: Case File — evidence-board interrogation cut
angles_discovered.hook: Coordinates, film stock codes, case numbers, and a face that resolves one plate at a time.
angles_discovered.why_now: The second supplied poster already speaks this language (FILM C-41, COORDINATES 35°41'N 139°46'E), so the copy is pre-written and the register is cold and procedural rather than the reference's velocity verbs.
grounded_in: Underserved gap: crime register in rapid-fire graphic grammar

angles_discovered.name: Three Prints — the poster triptych
angles_discovered.hook: The same frame, three different print treatments, cut against each other.
angles_discovered.why_now: The user supplied exactly three posters in three different treatments (illustrated, photographic, wide editorial). Cutting between treatments of one subject is the reference's own triptych move scaled up to the whole piece.
grounded_in: Reference shot 4 is a three-panel triptych

research_summary: The reference is a design piece, not a footage piece: twelve poster-frames in ten seconds, one hero glyph each, a strict two-accent palette on an achromatic base, a persistent print-artefact layer, and one signature trick — the character is depth-interleaved with the type, passing behind one letter and in front of the next. It resolves into a 2.5-second static lockup, which is what makes the preceding cutting legible rather than noisy. That grammar is fully reproducible in code with no image or video generation, which matters because this machine has 0 of 16 image providers and 0 of 26 video providers configured. The differentiation opportunity is register: the supplied posters are neo-noir crime, and crime titles almost never use rapid-fire graphic grammar — they default to slow and moody. A motionless subject inside a violently moving layout is the inversion the reference cannot perform, and the print mechanics in the posters (registration crosshair, duotone superimposition, halftone) give the motion an honest internal logic instead of arbitrary transitions.
